name: TaskManager
observations: Background task manager inspired by Celery and BullMQ
Features worker management, scheduled/cron jobs, live metrics, and dead letter queue
Target UI aligns with DESIGN.md Linear Dark design system
Feature ft-01-taskmanager-core completed with 20/20 tests passing and zero spec drift
Includes in-app worker spawner, backpressure guardrails, and Redis maintenance flush

name: BackendEngine
observations: Built with Python, FastAPI, and Redis
Manages job queueing, worker heartbeats, cron schedules, and WebSockets for real-time updates
Supports automated in-memory Redis fallback for zero-dependency development on Windows/macOS/Linux

name: FrontendDashboard
observations: Minimalist SPA dashboard built with modern vanilla JavaScript and CSS
Complies with DESIGN.md color palette (#010102 canvas, #5e6ad2 primary accent) and typography
Uses Linear Dark Toast notifications exclusively instead of browser alert() or confirm() popups
Provides real-time queue status table, Tempo trace timeline, Loki logs viewer, and Redis maintenance modal

name: RedisBroker
observations: Acts as the message broker and state storage for job queues, worker heartbeats, and pub/sub events
Includes atomic flush routines: flush_queues, flush_history, and flush_all

name: InAppWorkerManager
observations: Enables dynamic worker spawning via Web UI and REST API (/api/workers/spawn)
Supports pause, resume, and stop controls via Redis pub/sub commands
Implements resource guardrails for max CPU% and max RSS Memory MB with throttled backpressure

name: WindowsSubprocessUTF8
observations: Enforces PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 and PYTHONUTF8=1 in subprocess environments to prevent CP1252 UnicodeEncodeError with emojis on Windows

name: user:developer
observations: Prefers uv for Python package management, virtual environment isolation, and script running
Rejects browser alert/confirm popups in favor of modern toast notifications
Prefers managing workers and Redis maintenance directly from the Web UI
Developing in a Windows environment without hardware virtualization
